newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu "shocked" by hot tea attack on lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu "shocked" by hot tea attack on lawmaker.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accused of inciting right-wing passions before the killing of Yitzhak Rabin, rushed on Wednesday to express his shock after a religious Jew threw hot tea at a dovish lawmaker.

Israeli media on Wednesday were quick to link the scalding tea that a Jew in a skullcap splashed in legislator Yael Dayan's face in Hebron on Tuesday to the hollowed bullets another pumped into Prime Minister Rabin last November.

"The violence returns," read the front page of Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily. "Only the shortest distance separates this act of clear physical violence from the use of live weapons -- as short as the range of the gun which fired on Yitzhak Rabin," the newspaper said.
Israel this week marks the one-year anniversary of Rabin's assassination according to the Jewish lunar calendar.

A spokesman for Netanyahu said the right-wing Likud party leader telephoned Dayan on Wednesday to express his shock at the incident, which occurred while she led a peace tour of Hebron, in the West Bank.

"The prime minister strongly condemned violence in general and specifically that which occurs between people who differ politically," the spokesman said in a statement. "This cannot be the way to conduct a political argument."

Netanyahu's statements stood in sharp contrast to a resurrected file photo in Yedioth Ahronoth showing the smiling Likud party leader, then in opposition, leading a march of right-wing activists holding a coffin with Rabin's name on it.
Dayan, daughter of the late Israeli general Moshe Dayan, was treated for burns to her face and chest but did not require hospitalisation.
Her tea-throwing assailant, identified from television footage as an 60-year-old activist in the outlawed anti-Arab Kach party who was previously imprisoned for killing an Arab, is still at large.
"The little beast (Rabin assassin) Yigal Amir is in prison but the larger beast is still free," said Yossi Sarid, a legislator from the leftist Meretz party, alluding to political violence.
Dayan is a member of the opposition Labour party that signed a 1995 deal with the PLO providing for Israeli handover of most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.
Netanyahu, who opposed the Hebron deal, is locked in negotiations with the Palestine Liberation Organisation on the long-overdue army redeployment in the town.
The 400 Jewish settlers who live in heavily armed enclaves among 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron militantly oppose the planned troop pullback.
